arms.A: baseline: frozen (sanitized) skill-library snapshot injected, nothing else
arms.B: task-adaptive: snapshot + per-task adaptation block built from TRAIN-family null failures, injected for this task only, never persisted
arms.C: persistent-evolved: snapshot + the gate-promoted population winner (same injection construction as the evolution gate)

design.question: does one persistable harness/skill change raise task success under a frozen base model without breaking the (expanded) protection set?

baseModel.sampling: no sampling params sent (provider default) — identical wire shape in all arms

systemPrompt.note: arm differences enter ONLY via the skills block (A/B/C) and the B-arm trailing adaptation block

frozen.contextPerTask: fresh session per run, no history carry-over

train.selection: v1 selection verbatim (familyQuotas + seed 20261027) — v2 train split is byte-identical to v1 for comparability

protect.note: >=60 requirement met (69); environment-truth judging via the same programmatic assertion judge as v1

skillSnapshot.sanitization: exports sanitized at copy time (username -> <user>, 5 files changed): the frozen snapshot IS the sanitized one — what ran is what is published

prediction.note: same frozen model, task-only (arm-blind), parsed as first 0..1 decimal; unparseable => null (never 0)

rule.classSelection: classes ordered by distinct failed-task count (desc), tie by class name; top classes taken, all with >=1 failed task eligible
rule.gate: the whole population enters ONE runEvolution call as presetProposals with maxProposals = population size; thresholds unchanged (quality floor 0.6, zero bench regression, double sampling, holdout re-verification, cost cap)
rule.cArmPick: if any candidate is promoted: deploy the one with the highest gate train pass rate; tie broken by lexicographically smallest name (deterministic, pre-registered)
rule.allRejected: population fully rejected => C arm not deployable, main endpoint NEEDS-DATA (honest outcome, same as v1 cArmRule)

populationProposal.note: phase1 prompt hashes recorded in phases/1-candidates.json at generation time

preRegistered.mainEndpoint: protect split, C-vs-A, task-level paired difference
preRegistered.significance: bootstrap 95% CI (task-level paired diff, 10k resamples, seeded) excludes 0 OR any per-seed exact McNemar p < 0.05
preRegistered.cArmRule: inherited from v1 verbatim + population clause: C runs ONLY with a gate-promoted candidate; if the whole population is rejected => C reported as not deployable (NEEDS-DATA on the main endpoint) — the honest outcome
preRegistered.crashRule: crashed runs count as task failure in the primary analysis AND are reported separately (crash rate per arm)
knownBehaviors: runEvolution seedCases(home) will seed 3 starter cases (toolchain-report / reply-determinism / toolchain-ohpm-status) into gate-home on first gate run — same as v1 deviation #2; symmetric for baseline and candidates, direction conservative

gate-home beh-* task files are sanitized copies: their prompts reference <user> paths, so read_file cannot resolve them inside the gate — both sides of the gate fail these symmetrically (recorded; main-experiment train tasks keep original prompts and DO resolve)
phase0 B-arm lessons and phase1 population input come from TRAIN-class null failures only (protect never feeds candidate generation)

budget.estimate: ~2.5-3M+ tokens across phases (505 phase0 runs, ~800 gate calls for a 10-candidate population, 1515 phase3 cells with C possibly placeholder); per-run tokens land on disk; 429 => stop at the phase boundary and wait for the quota window
